prompt: Build the V8 demonstration with eight independent crank throws and closed cylinder bores: two banks at 45 degrees, eight distinct crank phases, one connected crankshaft on a main shaft, eight piston-and-rod sets on their own throws, and one connected crankcase block with eight closed cylinder bores (each with a cap at the head end), two main-bearing plates, one top rail, two head rails and four outboard columns. All eighteen instances must export separately and must not interfere at the five listed input angles.
notes: Contract v6 (closed-bore rung): eight independent throws at y = -91 + 26k with alternating +/-45 degree banks and phases 0/90/180/270/45/135/225/315; one connected crank on a single main shaft.

The frame is one connected crankcase block with eight closed cylinder bores (bore inner radius 10.1 mm, outer 12 mm, 1 mm cap at the head end), two main-bearing plates with journal bores at y = +/-98, a top rail, two head rails and four outboard columns into the base plate.

Bore clearance is a sampled radial gap between each slider and its closed bore wall (160 rays over 8 cylinders x 4 directions x 5 angles; inner radius 10.1 mm +/-0.1, gap 0.15-0.6 mm). Head clearance is the sampled axial gap between each piston and the bore cap/head rail, minimum 3.0-6.0 mm over 40 samples.
The main-bearing fit measures the two journal bores with the shared cylindrical-section measurement (0.2-0.6 mm diametral, axis offset at most 0.3 mm).

This is a demonstrator mechanism: no cylinder head with valves, ports or camshafts, no firing-order claim, no combustion, thermal, lubrication, load, wear or manufacturing claim. Only five sampled angles and 765 pairwise collision checks are covered.
